title: Networking & Linux for Security
summary: Learn TCP/IP, DNS, Linux fundamentals, command-line workflows, and troubleshooting.

lessons.title: TCP/IP and common network services
lessons.summary: Understand addressing, ports, DNS, HTTP, and TLS at a conceptual level.
lessons.content: Map a connection from name resolution to transport and application protocols. Use packet captures only in your own lab and minimize collection of sensitive traffic. Grasping the OSI 7-layer stack and TCP 3-way handshake is the foundational anchor for firewall configuration and traffic analysis.

quiz.question: What is DNS primarily used for?
options: Mapping names to records such as IP addresses
quiz.explanation: DNS resolves names and provides other published records; it is not an encryption protocol.

lessons.title: Linux permissions and process isolation
lessons.summary: POSIX permissions, UID/GID security models, and systemd service sandboxing.
lessons.content: Linux file modes (rwxrwxrwx), SUID/SGID bits, umask, and capabilities dictate execution boundaries. System services must execute as unprivileged service accounts with restrictive sandboxing flags.

quiz.question: Why is the SUID bit on an executable dangerous if misconfigured?
options: It deletes the binary on invocation
It causes the process to execute with the file owner's privileges rather than the caller's
quiz.explanation: SUID binaries execute with the permissions of the file owner (often root), creating high-risk privilege escalation avenues if flawed.
